hasPart.name: Recognizing a Layer 2 forwarding loop
teaches: Identify a possible switching loop from a broadcast surge and a source MAC address repeatedly learned on different ports.
Trace forwarding ports on the affected VLAN to find whether they form a closed path.

hasPart.name: Verifying the STP root bridge
teaches: Predict the root bridge for one spanning-tree instance from the switches’ bridge identifiers.
Compare the elected root with the intended root and explain an unexpected forwarding path after a switch is added.

hasPart.name: Interpreting spanning-tree port roles and states
teaches: Use root path costs and port roles to trace the active path and identify a redundant link held in reserve.
Determine whether a port can learn MAC addresses or forward user frames from its classic STP or RSTP state.

hasPart.name: Diagnosing an incorrect access VLAN
teaches: Compare the VLAN assigned to untagged traffic on a workstation’s port with the network plan.
Use the subnet of a DHCP lease together with the port’s VLAN membership to explain why a moved workstation reaches the wrong network.

hasPart.name: Tracing an ACL decision
teaches: Match an affected flow’s source, destination and service to the first applicable entry in an ordered ACL.
Use the interface, traffic direction and policy’s default action to explain a blocked flow. Confirm the matching rule with counters when available.

hasPart.name: Reading a routing table
teaches: Select the most specific matching prefix for a destination in an IPv4 forwarding table and identify its next hop or egress interface.
Trace a failed flow hop by hop and identify the first routing decision that sends it away from the intended destination.

hasPart.name: Diagnosing default route problems
teaches: Determine which destinations depend on the IPv4 default route when the routing table also contains specific routes.
Distinguish a missing default route from a default route with the wrong next hop by following traffic to an otherwise unmatched destination.

hasPart.name: Diagnosing DHCP address pool exhaustion
teaches: Use lease statistics to determine whether a DHCP scope has an IPv4 address available for a new client.
Distinguish an exhausted pool from a relay failure using the scope's free-address count and evidence that the client's request reached the DHCP server.

hasPart.name: Diagnosing an incorrect default gateway
teaches: Compare a host’s configured gateway with the intended router interface on its subnet.
Use reachability to a local peer, the intended gateway and a remote host to distinguish a host gateway error from an upstream routing failure.

hasPart.name: Identifying an incorrect IPv4 address
teaches: Use the documented subnet and host assignment to identify an endpoint configured with an address from the wrong subnet.
Distinguish a mistyped static address from a valid lease for the wrong VLAN by comparing the address source, switch port and address plan.

hasPart.name: Confirming a duplicate IPv4 address
teaches: Correlate a host’s address-conflict report with ARP evidence to identify two devices claiming the same IPv4 address on one link.
Use lease and static assignment records to select the conflicting assignment to correct and verify that each device has its intended address.

hasPart.name: Diagnosing an incorrect subnet mask
teaches: Apply the configured mask to the host and destination addresses to predict whether the host will use a gateway.
Compare that decision with the intended prefix and identify a mask that makes a remote host appear local or a local host appear remote.
